newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks weaker on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks weaker on profit-taking.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial shares traded largely weaker on continuing profit-taking in a subdued market on Thursday, brokers said.
The key industrial index lost 6.26 points to close at 7,963.93 on the back of a 450-cent fall to 2,800 on hotel and supermarkets group Meikles and banker Barclays' 200-cent drop to 2,200.
"The market was a bit weaker. There was some selling around. I think we are going to see the market coming off a bit," one broker said.
Dealers said an ongoing strike by junior doctors and other medical staff which has paralysed government hospitals had no effect on trade on the bourse.

Other losers included clothing retailer Truworths which shed 80 cents to 700, tobacco firm TSL which was 60 cents down to 620 and horticultural company Ariston and publishing group Zimpapers which each lost 50 cents to 1,500 and 2,050 respectively.
Against the trend, pork processor Colcom climbed 10 cents to 380 on the back of sturdy half-year results.
Sugar producer Hippo rose 25 cents to 925 while textiler David Whitehead, packaging firm Hunyani and seed manufacturer and distributor Seedco all added five cents to 70, 355 and 195 resepctively.
In minings, nickel producer Bindura and Wankie Colliery both traded unchanged while Falgold shed 10 cents to 130. The mining index ended 6.52 points lower at 1,230.25.
